full_judgment:
2. Brief facts are that the petitioner is a private limited company incorporated under the Companies Act having VAT Registration Certificate and engaged in the business of manufacturing GI Pipe and MS Pipe; In course of it's business, the petitioner submitted price declaration alongwith cost analysis on 18-1-2006 under Rule 3(1) of the Value Added Tax Rules, 1991 (hereinafter stated as 'VAT Rules') for it's products; Divisional Officer of the concern VAT Authority received the declaration on 23-1-2006; On 26-1-2006 respondent No. 3 Assistant Commissioner, Customs, Excise and VAT of the concern Division asked the petitioner to submit a new declaration for it's products and also informed that two sub-committees have been formed by the Commissioner of customs, Excise and VAT for fixing price of the MS Pipe and GI Pipe; On 2-5-2006, respondent No. 2 Commissioner, Customs, Excise and VAT Commissionerate, Dhaka (North), informed the Divisional Officers by a letter that the committee in their meeting has taken decision that the minimum value addition of the products fixed at 25% and directed to implement the decision within 15 days; Since Rule 3(3) of the VAT Rules provide that if no objection is raised within 15 days after receiving the declaration it would be deemed that the declaration has been accepted and accordingly the petitioner paying VAT regularly; Subsequently, the petitioner submitted another declaration on 23-5-2006 alongwith cost analysis for it's products which was received by the respondent No. 3 on 23-4-2006; Concern Divisional Officer of the VAT authority after receiving the price declaration most illegally approved the same by enhancing the price submitted by the petitioner vide order dated 31-5-2006 giving retrospective effect from 18-1-2006 in violation of the provisions of VAT Rules 3(3) beyond the statutory period of limitation without affording an opportunity of hearing. 

 15. It is settled that any law, circular, memo, promulgated/issued will take effect from the date of its promulgation or issuance. Even promulgation of any law without clearly enunciating that this law will take effect from a back date in that case also the law will take effect from the date of its promulgation. Promulgation of law is always take effect prospective unless giving retrospective effect in law itself with clear enunciation. As such approval of the declaration dated 23-5-2006 enhancing the value by giving retrospective effect from 18-1-2006 is not tenable in the eye of law. Furthermore, Rule 3(1) provides that the petitioner can supply its products on payment of VAT from the date of declaration for which rule 3(3) attached a condition of statutory period of limitation for 15 days after which it would be deemed that the VAT authority has no objection regarding price declaration submitted by the petitioner.
